Assignment instructions:
3.2 Assignment: Investigating circuits
Measurements in electric circuits change if the components are arranged in series or in parallel. How do they change?
By how much do they change?
The simulator allows you to build circuits and measure the potential difference and current. Your goal is to investigate
how either various number of battery cells or various number of loads (resistors or light bulbs) in both series and
parallel circuits change the potential difference and current.
Before you start, it would be a good strategy to read through the assignment to note what you will be doing and how
you might choose to organize your thinking
This assignment is worth 10% of your course grade.
Before you start, it would be a good strategy to read through the assignment to note what you will be doing and how
you might choose to organize your thinking. To complete this assignment, you will need access to the simulator titled
Circuit Construction, which is located in the Consolidation section of Learning Activity 3.2.
Instructions
To build your circuit, use the “Intro” part of the simulator. Begin by choosing if you will be investigating battery cells
(resistors) or loads (light bulbs).
Question
How does the potential difference and current change in different types of circuits?
Hypothesis
Which type of circuit will divide up the electric current? Which type of circuit will divide up the potential differences?
Be sure to justify your choice.
Materials
battery cells
wires
light bulbs
resistors
switches
Procedure
1. Choose if you will be using battery cells or various numbers of loads (resistors or light bulbs) to create your circuit.
Use your materials to create a series circuit.
2. Collect measurements for potential difference and current.
3. Make measurements for each of the components in the circuits.
4. Keep track of your results for each component in a table: the potential difference, the current, the brightness of
the lightbulb(s) (if you use any). Include a picture, diagram, description, or screenshot of how the circuits appear.
5. Repeat steps 1-4 for a parallel circuit.
Results
Summarize your observations of the two circuits in a table and notice any patterns you may have found.
Discussion
Use the results from your investigation to find a pattern.
1. How does electric current change in the circuits? Explain how the results show this.
2. How does potential difference change in the circuits? Explain how the results show this.
3. Do the measurements support Ohm’s law? Make a calculation for one component in your circuit to support your
answer.
4. Finally, use your understanding of electricity and circuits to explain the pattern you discovered.
Your teacher marker will grade and provide feedback on your work using the following success criteria and rubric.
Before submitting your assignment, review the success criteria and rubric. If you are unsure about how to format your
assignments, citation or what constitutes plagiarism, please review the following support pages:

Observations and results are organized in a table.
Answers to the questions include correctly interpreted results.
Answers to the questions are explained using concepts about electricity covered in the learning activity.
Relevant terminology, and correct spelling and grammar are used throughout.

Help me brainstorm ideas on what to write for this college application essay prompt. Make sure that you keep in mind what admissions officers really want to know and what can be good and memorable essays.

"Describe your most meaningful extracurricular activity"

right now I'm thinking about talking about my involvement with "House of Wisdom," a charity that I've worked with since 7th grade. It is based in Vietnam (my home country) and is focused on expanding education opportunities and providing education equity to rural and underprivileged communities across Vietnam, including my hometown of Ha Tinh. This is very meaningful to me because I can help the people in my community, my home country and hometown, the communities so close to who I am and where my roots are. They don't have a lot of opportunity, but for some reason, I was very lucky, and it was all based on luck, and I don't really think that's fair, so I want to help them. I also see so many talented kids and kids who actually want to learn and get an education but they don't have the opportunity to do so. Their houses don't have the internet or computers, they can barely afford books, and they have to travel arduous routes to get to their closest school, which can often be very under-resourced. I have been working since 7th grade with them in a few ways. I was pretty well-known back in Vietnam at the time due to my performances on a TV show captivating the country, with multiple videos gaining tens of millions of views. So part of what I did was I used my platform, to advocate and raise awareness for this initiative, I also used my social media to host memorabilia auctions of items from the gameshow and raised over $6,000. this has helped build many libraries and bring many books to their communities. I've come to some of their events, and talked at one and interacted with the kids at one of the house of wisdom franchises in my rural hometown of ha tinh. I've also taught many online classes for them in all different topics, from english to math, ai usage, my specialty of abacus arithmetic, and memorization methods. Now I am the Florida house of wisdom president. in the time that I've worked with them, we've grown massively to 350 house of wisdom centers built across 6 countries, and over 22,000 bookshelves/libraries built in 63 states across vietnam and laos.

let me know if you think this is a good idea to explore or if I should keep exploring other topics, and if you think this is a good topic, suggest some potential outlines.

Student Assignment Brief 
CONFIDENTIAL DOCUMENT 
This document is intended solely for Softwarica College of IT & E-Commerce students for their own use in completing their assessed work for this module. It must not be passed to third parties or posted on any website.  
Contents 
• 	Assignment Information

Assignment Information 
 
Module Name: 	Creative Thinking for Business   
Module Code: 	STA103IAE 
Assignment Title: 	Creativity applied in solving business problems  
Assignment Due: 	30 July 2025 
Assignment Credit: 	10 credits 
Word Count: 	2700 words ( +/- 10% ) 
Assignment Type: 	Case study report   
Grading: 	Percentage Grade (Applied Core Assessment) 
 
 
Assessment Overview 
You will be provided with an overall grade between 0% and 100%. You have one opportunity to pass the assignment at or above 40%. 
Important Notice 
The work you submit for this assignment must be your own independent work. More information is available in the 'Assignment Task' section of this assignment brief. 
Assessed Module Learning Outcomes 
 
The Learning Outcomes for this module align with the marking criteria which can be found at the end of this brief. Ensure you understand the marking criteria to ensure successful achievement of the assessment task. 
Learning Outcome 1: Reflect on their employability and creativity competencies and career management skills and plan for their future development. 
Learning Outcome 2: Demonstrate knowledge of idea generation techniques and creativity 
Learning Outcome 3: Apply knowledge to create a new venture or solve a problem 
Assignment Task 
Task Description:  
In this assignment, you are required to develop a comprehensive case study report proposing a new venture built around an innovative business idea. This should include the following key components: 
1.	Introduction to Business Idea (10%): Provide a brief introduction to your business idea, explaining the core concept and its purpose. Identify the specific problem your business aims to solve and describe your approach to addressing this issue. Discuss the role of creativity in designing and developing your business model, highlighting any unique or innovative strategies used.  
2.	Financial Planning and Budgeting (35%):  Discuss the financial aspects required to establish and sustain the startup. Provide a detailed breakdown of budgeting, including initial investment, revenue projections, and cost distribution. Explain the operational framework, covering key activities, logistics, and resource allocation. Outline the marketing strategy, focusing on customer acquisition, branding, and marketing positioning. Identify key stakeholders, such as investors, business partners, and advisors, and define their roles in the business. Present a structured timeline, highlighting key milestones and deadlines for implementation.  
3.	Business Case Analysis (15%): Evaluate your business model using various strategic frameworks. Conduct a SWOT analysis to assess strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats. Apply PEST analysis to examine political, economic, social, and technological factors affecting the business. Use the Value Proposition Canvas (VPC) to align customer needs with business value. Develop a Business Model Canvas (BMC) to outline essential components of your model. Perform a market analysis to understand industry trends, target audiences, and competition. Provide a product or service analysis, detailing features, differentiation, and value proposition. Highlight the application of ingenuity in solving market gaps and creating a competitive advantage.  
4.	Implementation and Challenges (15%): Assess the implementation process, examining the steps taken to bring the business idea to life. Use Mind maps to organize and identify key challenges encountered and explain how they were addressed. Discuss the application of ingenuity and problem-solving strategies in overcoming obstacles. Use the Systems Thinking Heuristic (STH) approach to provide a broader perspective on the implementation process and its overall impact.  
5.	Self-Reflection and Learning Outcomes (10%): Reflect on the impact of this project on personal growth, creativity, and problem-solving abilities. Explain how the experience has influenced your understanding of entrepreneurship and the industry. Discuss the skills and knowledge gained, including strategic thinking, financial planning, and business development. Provide insights into how this process has shaped your perspective on innovation and business strategy.  
6.	References and Citations (5%): Include a list of academic references, such as books, research papers, and credible websites, used to support your analysis. Ensure that all sources are properly cited following a recognized referencing style, such as APA or Harvard.  
7.	Presentation and Formatting (10%): Ensure the document is well-structured, with clear headings and logical organization. Maintain professional language, grammatical accuracy, and clarity throughout the report. Follow academic formatting guidelines, ensuring consistency in style and referencing.

sourceText:
below is the feedback I received from my supervisor related to a report that I had sent to him regarding the vulnerabilities in our environment. I am not clear as to what he is trying to say. Can you figure it out and help me understand point by point?

1) The overall format is good but the context is in between operations, tactical and strategical. E.g. there is no mentioning of report objectives, target audience, assumptions and scopes (both in scope and out of scope) so it's not clear who should read this and what to expect after reading through. 

2) from operations perspective, we've surfaced based on vuln but missed key info to drive outcomes, e.g. the final table there could be improved by adding a column there to show more details (attack vector, the impacted products, etc)

3) from both operations and governance's perspective, there are decisions made in the report where we might be questioned and will be asked to provide more reference along with the report. E.g. why we suggested 1-2 weeks time to patch? Did we reach out to the teams that own the actions and run consultation, with an agreed approach in writing in place? What was the criteria and process to make that decision? Does it match the current IS18 or other framework/standard WT follow etc. 

4) There is limited strategic risk posture discussion because there is lack of pattern analysis, for example, the final table is good as it shows some patterns (e.g. there are so many rocks in the current Microsoft suites, which one of them weigh the most? Does it mean when budget planning occurs, MS requires more funding to address some of these reported patterns?) 

5) The actions/recommendations need to be more suitable for WT environment, and requires to be scoped in a granular level, e.g. Health assets or QRT-managed assets we are talking about here in this report. Some of the recommendations are too generic so you could put them in any report and they would read fine which is not what we want here. 

6) Also notably, there is no consideration of how current VMS operations occur in CG and what's the current patching cadence and criteria to prioritize vulnerability response effort, e.g. short term improvement (1-3 months), we suggested to focus on CVSS above or equal to 9 plus those known to be exploited in the wild, what does our VMS function suggest? Do we only consider CVSS and exploitation probability? Another example that we are not considering WT that much here can be the key concerns of REC, for example, we've put Windows servers there at highest risk, however, there is no mentioning of why the Windows servers were grouped along with desktops (i assumed you meant workstations here btw) but most of eHealth-managed servers cannot be reached unless you are inside WT network already.
